pages.text: "When's the boat coming, Mom?" Dari watched the sea from the dock. "Grandma's visiting from the mainland today." Dari tilted his head. "I can't quite remember her face..."
Kkiruk called, "A boat!" Grandma stepped off a white boat with a huge cloth-wrapped bundle. "My Dari!" He shyly hid behind Mom. "Hello..." A tiny voice.
Grandma opened her bundle on the kitchen table. Unfamiliar things, a mainland smell. Dari fidgeted with his flippers in a corner. "I only want Mom..." He felt glum.
Grandma set down a basket of strawberries. "Try one, little one. I picked them this morning." Her flippers were warm. Dari bit in, and sweetness spread through his mouth.

She took his flipper and led him to the vegetable patch. Strawberry seedlings had come from the bundle, too. "Plant one?" Dari tucked it into the soil. "Strawberries on our island, too?" Grandma chuckled.
Mom whispered, "Grandma spent days packing for your visit." Favorite snacks filled the bundle, along with a picture of baby Dari. She had thought about him so much. His heart stirred.
Dari hurried into her arms. "Hug me, Grandma!" Her hug was the softest, warmest in the world. "Grandma's the best!" He slapped his tail.
That evening, the lighthouse lamp lit. They gathered beside the kitchen stove: Grandma's mainland stories, Mom's seaweed soup. Dari laughed in Grandma's arms. She wasn't unfamiliar anymore.

Next day, Grandma boarded for the mainland. Tears stung Dari's eyes. Now he knew three things for her visits. "One, a loud hello! Two, sit beside Grandma! Three, a snuggly hug!" He put a shell necklace around her neck. "Come again!"
The boat drifted away. Dari waved his flippers high from the dock. Mom hugged him from behind. "You love Grandma now!" Sharing love had brought them close. "Grandma's the best!"
